requirements.evidence: Every contract item is present: locale/name in `.env.example:1-8` and `phpunit.xml:22-24`; theme config `config/mail.php:131-137`; brand colour on the action button `resources/views/vendor/mail/html/themes/pegafila.css:240-247` (`background-color: #0f7490`); routes `routes/web.php:16-31` (`password.request/email/reset/update`, `verification.verify` with `auth`, `signed`, `throttle:6,1`); reset logic `app/Http/Controllers/NewPasswordController.php:30-50` (forceFill password + remember_token, `PasswordReset`, redirect `/`); rules `app/Http/Requests/ResetPasswordRequest.php:27-33` (token, email, min 8/letters/mixedCase/numbers/confirmed); verification `app/Http/Controllers/Auth/VerifyEmailController.php:18-27`; subject translations `lang/pt_BR.json:559,804`.

conventions.evidence: Follows the controller/FormRequest split (`ResetPasswordRequest` for three rules, inline validate for the one-field forgot form at `app/Http/Controllers/PasswordResetLinkController.php:29-31`), reuses Laravel's broker/`EmailVerificationRequest`, and updates the changelog (`CHANGELOG.md:15-25`). The visible deviation is the duplicated full-page shell in both new views (`resources/views/auth/forgot-password.blade.php:1-16` and `resources/views/auth/reset-password.blade.php:1-16`) instead of an anonymous Blade component.

security.evidence: Verification is authorized through `EmailVerificationRequest` (signed URL plus id/hash `hash_equals`) at `app/Http/Controllers/Auth/VerifyEmailController.php:18-27`; both sensitive routes are throttled (`routes/web.php:19-21,29-31`); forgot-password always returns the same `passwords.sent` flash for known and unknown addresses (`app/Http/Controllers/PasswordResetLinkController.php:29-35`); all input is validated server-side (`ResetPasswordRequest.php:27-33`); output is escaped (`{{ $token }}` at `resources/views/auth/reset-password.blade.php:28`, `{{ session('status') }}`); no mass-assignment exposure (`forceFill` with explicit keys).

tests.evidence: Feature tests cover locale/env/theme (`tests/Feature/AppLocaleTest.php:3-25`), both translated e-mails and the inlined brand button (`tests/Feature/AccountEmailsTest.php:10-48`), reset happy path/non-enumeration/throttle/invalid and cross-account token/password rules (`tests/Feature/Auth/PasswordResetTest.php`), and verification success, id/hash mismatch, tampered/unsigned/expired links and throttling (`tests/Feature/Auth/VerifyEmailTest.php`). No existing tests are weakened.

simplicity.evidence: The implementation reuses Laravel's notifications, password broker, `EmailVerificationRequest` and a FormRequest rather than adding abstractions. The main unnecessary repetition is the ~30-line document shell copied into both views (`resources/views/auth/forgot-password.blade.php:1-16`, `resources/views/auth/reset-password.blade.php:1-16`).

readability.evidence: Small, documented controller actions (`app/Http/Controllers/NewPasswordController.php:16-50`), clearly named request rules, and accessible labelled inputs with `aria-invalid`/`aria-describedby` (`resources/views/auth/forgot-password.blade.php:37-54`, `reset-password.blade.php:30-48`). No dead code or debug output.

scope.evidence: Every changed file serves the task: `.env.example`, `phpunit.xml`, `config/mail.php`, the `pegafila` theme, `lang/pt_BR.json`, routes, the three controllers, the form request, the two auth views, the tests and `CHANGELOG.md`. No unrelated refactors or out-of-scope features (login, registration, `/home`, Livewire, layouts) were added.

issues.explanation: Both views duplicate the same document head, fonts/vite-CDN branch and Bulma wrapper; extracting that shell into an anonymous Blade component would avoid the copy-paste (a full layout is correctly out of scope).
Only the forgot-password form is tested against the `guest` middleware; `password.reset` and `password.update` are also in the guest group but have no authenticated-user test.
The return value of `markEmailAsVerified()` is ignored and `Verified` is fired unconditionally; the usual Breeze pattern only fires the event when the update succeeded.
A global `const NEW_PASSWORD` and a global `signedVerificationUrl()` helper leak into the shared test namespace and could collide as the suite grows; keep them local or static.

The status assertions reuse `__('passwords.sent')`/`__('passwords.reset')`, the same expression the controllers use, so a missing pt_BR `passwords.*` translation (flash rendering literally as `passwords.sent`) would not be caught.

review.summary: The change implements the pt-BR account e-mails: locale/name pins, the `pegafila` mail theme with the #0f7490 action button, translated ResetPassword/VerifyEmail notifications, the guest password-reset endpoints (throttled, non-enumerating, remember-token rotation, PasswordReset event) and the signed id/hash verification endpoint, with broad Pest coverage. It meets the task and is secure; I would approve it with a few nits, mainly the duplicated page shell in the two new views and a couple of small test-quality gaps.
